payload.reasoning_summary: FASE-1 is the earliest incomplete phase, and the repository lacks its prerequisite monorepo, build, test, lint, and dependency-boundary foundation. The prior pnpm-based bootstrap repeatedly failed in the authoritative environment, so the highest-value legal unit is a clean npm-workspaces bootstrap. ADR-dependent algorithms and later FASE-1 domain features remain premature.
risks: A workspace or TypeScript-project count inferred from directory layout may diverge if non-TypeScript mandated workspaces are handled inconsistently; tests must enumerate explicit expected paths rather than merely assert a count.
Boundary resolution can accidentally miss relative imports or authorize transitive dependencies; dedicated negative fixtures are required.
Dependency installation may still fail if the committed lockfile is not generated with the npm version used by the authoritative environment.
An empty blocker registry must not be interpreted as resolution of already identified specification ambiguities; those affected implementation fronts remain out of scope and blocked.

acceptance_criteria: The root package.json declares npm workspaces for all 16 mandated directories, and each directory exists with valid workspace metadata.
A committed package-lock.json is present, and npm ci succeeds from a clean checkout in the authoritative validation environment.
No pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm shim, pnpm packageManager declaration, or pnpm invocation exists in repository-controlled configuration, scripts, source, or CI.
The exact root commands npm run compile, npm run lint, npm run boundary, and npm run test each exit 0 after npm ci.
Every TypeScript workspace configuration extends the shared base configuration, and the effective configuration enables strict and noUncheckedIndexedAccess.
TypeScript source discovery and relevant gates cover .ts, .tsx, .mts, and .cts files.
The pure-package lint restrictions apply to all four TypeScript extensions under packages/; any exception is confined to packages/adapters or packages/ui as allowed by the specification.

The boundary checker rejects forbidden direct cross-workspace imports, including relative cross-workspace imports, while permitting only direct edges declared by §14.5 and not treating transitive reachability as permission.
CI uses npm ci and runs compile, lint, boundary, and test successfully against committed state.
SPEC_BLOCKERS.md exists with the fields required by §19 and does not record a fabricated resolution.
No production algorithm, economic behavior, or behavior dependent on an unresolved DEFINIR item is introduced.
must_preserve: The authority and contents of CICLO_SPEC.md and BENCHMARK.md.
All existing benchmark history, checkpoints, and accepted repository state.
Direct-edge semantics of the §14.5 dependency graph.
The prohibition on silently resolving contradictions or DEFINIR items.
Deterministic, strict, and noUncheckedIndexedAccess TypeScript foundations.
Zero production domain or economic behavior during bootstrap.
task.objective: Establish an installable, deterministic TypeScript monorepo foundation whose compile, lint, boundary, and test gates pass using npm only.
out_of_scope: pnpm configuration, lockfiles, shims, commands, or package-manager fallback behavior.
Production algorithms, economic rules, simulation behavior, persistence formats, RNG, canonical encoding, or state hashing.
ADRs resolving DEFINIR items, including ADR-002, ADR-004, and ADR-009.
Implementation of packages/world, packages/domain, packages/application, replay behavior, or benchmarks.
Resolution of the transcendental-function contradiction, octave parameters, or tools dependency-edge ambiguity.
Dependency rules for tools/* that are not explicitly defined by §14.5.
required_tests: A configuration test enumerates every mandated TypeScript project and verifies inheritance of strict and noUncheckedIndexedAccess plus coverage of .ts, .tsx, .mts, and .cts.
Negative lint fixtures using .mts and .cts demonstrate that prohibited pure-package constructs fail the real lint gate.

Boundary tests demonstrate rejection of a forbidden direct edge, rejection of an attempted edge justified only by transitive reachability, and rejection of a relative import crossing into a disallowed workspace.
A positive boundary test demonstrates acceptance of at least one explicitly allowed direct edge.
Clean-install validation runs npm ci followed by npm run compile, npm run lint, npm run boundary, and npm run test.
scope: Configure the repository root as an npm workspaces monorepo with a committed package-lock.json and the 16 directories mandated by §14.4 registered as workspaces.
Add root npm scripts named compile, lint, boundary, and test, with no pnpm dependency or invocation.
Create the shared strict TypeScript configuration and minimal per-project configurations for every mandated TypeScript workspace, covering .ts, .tsx, .mts, and .cts sources.
Implement lint configuration enforcing §13 pure-package restrictions across all four TypeScript extensions, with exceptions limited to the specification-authorized adapters and UI locations.
Implement a dependency-boundary checker that validates direct imports against the directed graph in §14.5, including relative imports that cross workspace boundaries.
Add CI configuration that installs with npm ci and runs the four required root gates.
Create SPEC_BLOCKERS.md in the §19 registry format without inventing, resolving, or implementing any specification decision.
Add only minimal non-domain placeholder sources needed to make the workspace and gates executable.
task.title: Bootstrap the FASE-1 monorepo with npm workspaces and architecture gates
